title: How AI Learns
hook: Training an AI is like teaching by flashcards on a massive scale: show it an example, let it guess, tell it how wrong it was, and nudge it to do better — billions of times.
key_points: Models learn by guessing, getting corrected, and adjusting — repeated at huge scale.
They need enormous amounts of example data to find reliable patterns.
What they learn is only as good as the examples they're shown.
After training, using the model ('inference') is fast — the slow, costly part is learning.
content_html: Imagine teaching a child to recognize dogs by showing them thousands of photos. At first they guess wildly; each time you say "yes" or "no," and slowly they get it. AI learns the same way, just at a scale no human could match. The system makes a guess, gets told how far off it was, and makes a tiny adjustment to do better next time — then repeats that loop millions or billions of times until the guesses get good.
extra_html: This is why data matters so much. A model only knows the world through the examples it was trained on, so the quality and variety of that data quietly shape everything it does — including its blind spots. Two other things are worth knowing. First, training is the expensive, slow part (huge amounts of computing power and energy); once a model is trained, using it is comparatively quick and cheap. Second, a trained model is essentially frozen — it doesn't keep learning from your conversations unless its makers deliberately retrain it, which is why a chatbot may not know about very recent events.

related.title: What AI Actually Is
related.hook: AI isn't a thinking robot — it's software that learns patterns from huge piles of examples, then uses them to make a good guess about something new.

related.title: Generative AI
related.hook: The AI behind ChatGPT and image generators doesn't look up answers — it predicts what plausibly comes next, one piece at a time, until it has built a whole response.

related.title: Bias & Fairness
related.hook: AI learns from data made by people, so it inherits our patterns — including the unfair ones. A model trained on a biased past will confidently recommend a biased future.

related.title: Kids Outlearn AI — and Nobody Knows Why
related.hook: A toddler masters a language from a few years of overheard chatter. A chatbot needs a large fraction of the written internet. Nobody can fully explain the gap.

flashcards.prompt: In one sentence, how does an AI model learn?
flashcards.back_html: It guesses, gets told how wrong it was, and makes a tiny adjustment — repeated over and over across huge amounts of example data.

flashcards.prompt: Why might a chatbot not know about very recent events?

choices.text: A trained model is frozen and doesn't keep learning unless it's retrained
It forgets recent information every night
It only checks the news on weekends

flashcards.explanation_html: Training is a one-time, expensive step. Afterwards the model is essentially frozen — it won't know newer events unless its makers retrain it.
